en: Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Śrāvastī, in the Samantaprāsāda, together with a great community of monks consisting of twelve hundred and fifty monks, with immeasurable bodhisattva mahāsattvas headed by Avalokiteśvara, and with many hundreds of thousands of those to be trained. With his body unmoving, the Blessed One sat upon a lion throne of jewels.

2. Then indeed, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī, through the power of the Buddha, rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee upon the ground, and bowing with palms joined toward the Blessed One, addressed the Blessed One as follows:

3. "Blessed One, what is the measure of that great merit by which, through such great merit, the Tathāgata’s Dharma-conch becomes the fulfillment of the intentions of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of those to be trained?"

When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta: “Mañjuśrī, inconceivable is this great merit consisting of wisdom and permeated by great compassion; by means of this great merit, the Tathāgata’s Dharma-conch becomes the fulfillment of the intentions of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of those to be trained.”

5. Mañjuśrī, suppose all the sentient beings in Jambudvīpa were to be endowed with the ten paths of wholesome action; if one were to take the mass of merit belonging to all those sentient beings and multiply that very mass of merit by a hundred, it would equal the merit of a king who is the sovereign lord of Jambudvīpa.

6. Mañjuśrī, suppose all the beings in Jambudvīpa were each endowed with the mass of merit belonging to the lord of Jambudvīpa; and suppose that by a mass of merit equal to the combined merit of all those beings, multiplied a hundredfold, one becomes a universal monarch (cakravartin), the sovereign lord of the four continents, endowed with the seven treasures. These are his seven treasures:

Namely: the wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the jewel-treasure, the woman-treasure, the householder-treasure, and the counselor-treasure as the seventh. He also has a thousand sons who are brave, heroic, handsome in form, and crushers of enemy armies. In this way, Mañjuśrī, such is a universal monarch (cakravartin), possessed of great supernatural power and great majesty.

7. Mañjuśrī, suppose all the sentient beings in a four-continent world-system were each endowed with the mass of merit of a universal monarch; the mass of merit belonging to all those sentient beings, multiplied a thousandfold, constitutes Śakra, the lord of the gods. Thus is Śakra, the lord of the gods, possessed of such great supernatural power and great majesty.

8. Mañjuśrī, suppose all the beings in a world-system of four continents were endowed with the mass of merit of Śakra; the mass of merit belonging to all those beings, by that very same mass of merit [multiplied] a hundred thousand times—
